title.narrative: Strengthened capacity of member States to ratify and apply international labour standards and to fulfil their reporting obligations

description.narrative: Egypt is currently revising its labor law, with the draft undergoing discussions in the House of Representatives. The ILO provided informal comments in 2023 and formal comments in 2024 to ensure better alignment with ratified ILO conventions. In a significant step, Egypt ratified the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC, 2006) in 2024, its first ILO Convention ratification since 2004. This ratification follows approval by both the President and Parliament in June 2023. ILO's International Labour Standards (ILS) activities in Egypt are focused on promoting stronger application of existing conventions and encouraging new ratifications. Current and planned efforts include comparative analyses for C. 122 (Employment Policy), C. 155/187 (OSH fundamental conventions), and potentially P. 29 (Forced Labour). Support for ratifying C. 185 (Seafarer's Documents) may resume once specific clarification on identity document requirements is addressed. Collaboration with the National Centre for Judicial Studies continues until September 2024, aiming for judicial rulings that directly reference ILS, as seen previously. Support for labor law legal aid centers is also under consideration. Egypt has ratified 64 ILO conventions, with 57 currently in force. Notably, it has not ratified key conventions like the OSH fundamental conventions or P. 29, nor governance convention No. 122. The ongoing comparative analyses are expected to reinvigorate interest in these ratifications. A review of the 57 in-force conventions is also planned, as some are outdated and ideally require replacement with more current standards, potentially with support from RBTC resources.
